question: To what extent can a designation remain applicable despite an underlying unity?
premises: A designation may be applicable in some contexts.
Such applicability arises only to a limited extent.
Contextual usefulness does not negate underlying unity.
inference: A designation holds only insofar as it serves a contextual purpose within an underlying unity.
uncertainties: The exact antecedent of the limited applicability depends on the preceding verses.
plain_english: It is applicable in some cases only to that extent, thus.
